I would keep my land in the wheat-maize rotation this year. In Quzhou County, that is the cropping pattern I trust most because it fits the local climate, the irrigation conditions, and the way I know how to farm. I am 60, so I would not make the year more complicated by dividing the land into many small crops. I would plant winter wheat on all of my land, then follow it with summer maize on the same fields after harvest. I would use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed because I would want stable emergence, better stress tolerance, and higher yield than old saved seed. For tillage, I would plough or rotary-till before wheat to prepare a clean seedbed, then I would use no-tillage or very light disturbance for maize after wheat harvest so I can save labor and get the summer crop in quickly. I would use moderate fertilizer rather than pushing too hard, because grain is important but I would still want to control cost and avoid wasting fertilizer. I would irrigate wheat more than maize, since wheat in this area depends more on timely watering, especially at jointing and grain filling. I would spray only as needed but I would still plan a small number of pesticide applications because aphids, rust, armyworm, and corn borers are common enough that I would not leave the crop unprotected. Assuming I manage about 10 mu, I would put the full 10 mu into this double-cropping system because it is the safest and most familiar way for me to secure grain and income.
